answer_part:
The CONTROL device formulation employs PiPI at 0.15 mg/mL alongside PDADI (0.5 mg/mL) in the passivation layer, which introduces interfacial limitations despite adequate bulk perovskite passivation. PiPI's presence creates an overly thick or disordered organic layer at the perovskite/hole-transport interface, increasing series resistance and impeding hole extraction. This manifests as a suboptimal fill factor (77.03%) due to charge accumulation and enhanced non-radiative recombination at grain boundaries. While PiPI nominally passivates surface defects, its molecular structure likely causes steric hindrance with the underlying 4,4,4-NA SAM, disrupting energy level alignment and reducing hole mobility. The resulting voltage losses lower the open-circuit voltage (1.138 V) below theoretical limits, as unmitigated trap-assisted recombination persists at the interface. Removing PiPI eliminates this parasitic resistance while retaining sufficient defect passivation from PDADI alone, which selectively binds to undercoordinated Pb²⁺ ions without compromising interfacial kinetics. Although complete PiPI removal risks minor under-passivation of iodide vacancies, the trade-off favors improved charge transport, as PDADI’s optimal concentration (0.5 mg/mL) maintains surface defect suppression while enabling efficient hole transfer to the SAM. This adjustment directly targets the primary failure mode of interfacial recombination and resistive losses, elevating both voltage and fill factor without altering perovskite crystallization or bulk morphology.

The CONTROL device achieves a power conversion efficiency of 21.89% with a short-circuit current density of 24.96 mA/cm², open-circuit voltage of 1.138 V, and fill factor of 77.03%. The optimized formulation increases the open-circuit voltage to the range of 1.16 V, short-circuit current density to 25.39–25.79 mA/cm², and fill factor to 83.87–85.87%, yielding a power conversion efficiency of 24.70–25.69%. These gains stem from reduced interfacial recombination losses and lower series resistance, directly attributable to the refined passivation strategy.

Implement the following formulation changes:  
- Eliminate PiPI from the passivation layer solution.  
- Maintain PDADI concentration at 0.5 mg/mL in ethanol for the passivation layer.  
- Retain all other composition variables unchanged, including perovskite stoichiometry (Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅I₃ at 1.65 mol/L), precursor additives (MACl at 15.0 mg/mL, p-F-PEACl at 2.0 mg/mL), and SAM (4,4,4-NA at 0.5 mg/mL).
control_device_fabrication: A significantly higher JSC of 24.9648 mA/cm² is obtained while preserving VOC of 1.13828 V and FF of 77.029%, resulting in the highest PCE of 21.8893% at reverse scan. For the Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85I3, 1.65 mol/L perovskite precursor solution was prepared. A SAM solution consisting of 4,4,4-NA (0.5 mg/mL) in ethanol was prepared. The addition of MACl (15.0 mg/mL) and p-F-PEACl (2.0 mg/mL) were then completed. The perovskite film was deposited by spin-coating at 1000 rpm for 5 s and 5500 rpm for 30 s. During the spin-coating, 150 µL CB solution was dripped at 15 s before ending. Heat-treatment was implemented with the substrates for 15 min at 110 °C. To enhance device performance, PDADI (0.5 mg/mL) and PiPI (0.15 mg/mL) were deposited as a passivation layer on the sample surface using spin-coating. The passivation mixed solution was spin-coated on the perovskite films at 5000 rpm for 30 s. At 6 s, a drop of 70 µL passivator was introduced during spin-coating. Passivator solution was spin-coated and annealed at 100 ℃ for 5 min. In details, SAM solution was spin-coated on the substrate at 3000 rpm for 30 s, and annealed at 100 °C for 10 min.
target_device_fabrication: A higher PCE of 25.7614% is achieved with JSC of 25.5903 mA/cm², VOC of 1.1862 V, and FF of 84.8668%. With Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85I3 at 1.65 mol/L forming the primary solution, the perovskite precursor was synthesized accordingly. The hole transport layer (HTL) was fabricated using the SAM solution of 4,4,4-NA. The 4,4,4-NA concentration is 0.5 mg/mL. During solar cell device fabrication, MACl (15.0 mg/mL), and p-F-PEACl (2.0 mg/mL) were added to the precursor solution. Implementing a stepwise spin scheme, the layer was first spun at 1000 rpm (5 s) and then at 5500 rpm (30 s), improving surface coverage. A total of 150 µL of CB was slowly dripped onto the center of film at 15 s before the end of spin-coating. The perovskite layer was thermally conditioned at 110 °C for 15 min, consolidating its morphology. For better device performance, a passivation layer of PDADI (0.5 mg/mL) was deposited through spin-coating. The passivation layer was applied via spin-coating at 5000 rpm for 30 s. The addition of 70 µL passivator occurred at 6 s during spin-coating. Then, it was annealed at 100 ℃ for 5 min. In details, SAM solution was spin-coated on the substrate at 3000 rpm for 30 s, and annealed at 100 °C for 10 min.
